title: Lantern Depths – A Roguelike Where the Light Runs Out
tools: JavaScript (canvas, no engine) · SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) with a Pixel Art XL LoRA (low-rank adaptation)
blurb: A small turn-based roguelike in a single HTML (HyperText Markup Language) file. Every step burns lamp oil, the light radius shrinks as it drains, and at zero the dark starts to hurt. Sprites were generated locally with SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) and a pixel-art LoRA (low-rank adaptation).
long: Lantern Depths is a turn-based dungeon crawl in plain JavaScript and canvas, one index.html with no engine. Each floor is generated fresh; you descend by finding the stairs before the lamp fails. Oil is the clock: the light radius drops from 5 tiles to 4, then 3 as it drains, and with an empty lamp the dark damages you every few turns.

Between floors you pick one of three blessings from a pool of nine (more health, a polished lens for light radius, slower-burning wick, heal on kill and others). Embers carried out of a run buy permanent camp upgrades, saved in the browser. Five monster types appear by depth, including lamp moths that drink your oil and shades that fear the light.

The pixel-art sprites for the player, monsters and items came from a local generation pipeline: SDXL (Stable Diffusion XL) with the Pixel Art XL and LCM (latent consistency model) LoRAs (low-rank adaptations), a border flood-fill to key out the background, then a bake step that packs the chosen sprites into the page.
highlights: Single HTML (HyperText Markup Language) page, no game engine
Light radius 5 → 4 → 3 tiles as oil drains
9 blessings, 5 monster types, persistent camp upgrades
